brand_notes.fabric: brands.json's brand-level fabric string is 'TPU laminate (shiny welded) truck-tarp material with Cordura panels'. Checked all five catalogued products against Chrome's own materials copy and this is a patchwork average, not accurate for any single product: (1) Holman Handlebar Bag and Holman Top Tube Bag: maker copy says 'Made from recycled X fabric' - Chrome's own branded laminate, visually a slightly glossy ripstop consistent with a TPU-look face in photos, but these are conventional ZIPPERED bags, not welded construction, so the 'shiny welded' half is wrong for these two. (2) Holman Pannier: '600D recycled polyester with 150D recycled polyester liner', described only as 'weather resistant' - no TPU, no welding, no Cordura anywhere in the copy; the weakest match of the five. (3) Urban Ex 2.0 Pannier: '600D Polyester with PU coating on surface and TPU backing, 70D Polyester lining', and the feature list explicitly says '100% welded waterproof' - this is the ONE product that actually earns the 'TPU laminate (shiny welded)' half of the brand string, confirmed by photos showing true dry-bag rolltop construction. (4) Doubletrack Saddle Roll: 'Bluesign approved 1050D nylon with 500D tarp liner' - the 'tarp liner' phrase is the closest thing to 'truck-tarp material' in the whole catalogue and is a genuine match. 'Cordura' does not appear in ANY of the five products' own materials text - it may describe a different Chrome product line (their messenger bags) but is not confirmed for anything in this catalogue.
brand_notes.method: No local photo folder for this brand. Two of five products (Holman Handlebar Bag, Holman Top Tube Bag) are live on chromeindustries.com and were fetched two ways: the Shopify '.json' product endpoint (clean structured data - title, body_html, variant list, full image CDN URLs) and a plain curled HTML page (for the accordion copy the .json endpoint omits - full feature bullets and the 'Sizing & Materials' dimensions block). The other three (Holman Pannier, Urban Ex 2.0 Pannier, Doubletrack Saddle Roll) are NOT in Chrome's current product/collection listings as of this review (Aug 2026) - `products.json` and the 'bags' collection no longer list them, and the live product.json endpoints 404. All three were recovered from the Wayback Machine (web.archive.org), which had snapshots from January 2026 (Holman Pannier), March 2025 (Doubletrack), and 2023 (Urban Ex 2.0, under its actual slug 'waterproof-urban-ex-2-0-pannier' - the catalogue's assumed slug 'urban-ex-pannier-2-0' never existed). This means all three still describe real, previously-sold Chrome products with genuine maker dimensions/materials/photos, but their current-catalogue status is worth a second look - not something I've changed, since these are still legitimate bike-mounted bags unlike Rapha's off-bike Essentials Bag flagged by another reviewer, just noting the risk that Chrome may no longer sell them.

products.name: Holman Pannier
products.dims_raw: Maker Sizing accordion (via Wayback snapshot): 'Height: 15.5" | Width: 11.5" top - 10.75" base | Depth: 5"', Volume 15-20 Liters, Strap length 31-59in.
products.dims_note: UNCHANGED from the catalogue's existing (already-corrected) figures, now independently re-confirmed against the maker's own spec text rather than the third-party retailer listings the catalogue previously cited. Height (the vertical hang axis) maps to hgt (15.5in=39.4cm), Width (fore-aft along the rack, tapering 11.5in top to 10.75in base) maps to len using the larger/top value per the tapered-axes rule (29.2cm), Depth maps to wid (5in=12.7cm). This is a fixed-size messenger-flap bag, not a rolltop, so there is no unfurled/min-height ambiguity to apply.

geometry.notes: Vertical rectangular messenger-bag-style pannier, taller than wide - NOT a rolltop dry bag like its Urban Ex sibling. Flap top with two side-release buckles, front zip pocket, fabric top carry handle, and a long adjustable/removable shoulder strap for off-bike carry.

closure.hardware: two side-release buckles on webbing straps over a messenger-style flap

details.seams: described only as 'weather resistant', not welded/waterproof like the Urban Ex 2.0 - see brand_notes.fabric
details.fabric: 600D recycled polyester with 150D recycled polyester liner - see brand_notes.fabric

mount.notes: Hangs from a rear rack via 'universal mounting hardware' (hook/rail clips on the rear face, not visible in the studio photo available) - requires a rack, so flagged fits:rack_only rather than left in the universal pool. Soft-bodied bag, hangs vertically, no internal rigid frame visible.

products.name: Urban Ex Pannier 2.0
products.dims_raw: Maker Sizing accordion (via Wayback snapshot): 'Height: 18-23" | Width: 12" | Depth: 6"', Volume/Capacity 17-21L.
products.dims_note: AXIS-SWAP CORRECTION - the same defect the brief warns about, and the same one already caught and fixed on this pannier's Holman sibling but missed here. The existing catalogue had len:58.4 (mapping the maker's 23in maximum HEIGHT into the length axis) and hgt:15.2 (mapping the 6in DEPTH into height) - that draws the pannier lying on its side, on a random axis, with its actual vertical extent reduced to a slab 15cm tall. Correct mapping, consistent with the Holman Pannier correction: Height (18-23in, the vertical hang axis - and here it is a genuine RANGE, since this is a rolltop) maps to hgt using the new MINIMUM-of-range rule = 18in = 45.7cm; Width (12in, fore-aft along the rack) maps to len = 30.5cm; Depth (6in, thickness against the rack) maps to wid = 15.2cm. Volume check: 30.5 x 15.2 x 45.7 = 21.2L box against the 17-21L rating - a clean 1.0x match at the rolled-down minimum, which is exactly what the minimum-height rule is supposed to produce, so no render override is needed here.

geometry.notes: True rolltop dry-bag pannier, taller than wide, hangs from a rack via a hook/clip visible at the top rear. Three horizontal compression straps across the front face, a diagonal reflective accent stripe down one side, small Chrome box-logo tag low on the front.

closure.hardware: side-release buckle at the roll; maker copy: '100% welded waterproof lightweight single pannier'

details.reflective: diagonal accent stripe on one side panel
details.seams: welded (maker copy: '100% welded waterproof lightweight single pannier')
details.fabric: 600D Polyester with PU coating on surface and TPU backing, 70D Polyester lining - see brand_notes.fabric; the one product in this brand's catalogue that actually matches brands.json's 'TPU laminate (shiny welded)' description

mount.notes: Adjustable locking hook hardware clips onto rack tubing 6-12mm diameter per maker copy. Requires a rack - flagged fits:rack_only. Soft dry-bag body, hangs from the top hook.

products.name: Doubletrack Saddle Roll
products.dims_raw: Maker Sizing accordion (via Wayback snapshot): 'Height: 6.25" | Width: 3.5" rolled - 10" unrolled', Weight 0.26lbs.
products.dims_note: Refined from the existing catalogue estimate (len 15.5, dia 7.9) using the maker's own figures. This is a flat panel that rolls into a tube and buckles shut, similar in construction logic to Alpkit's Airlok Dual: the maker's 'Height' (6.25in=15.9cm) is the FIXED long axis of the roll (mapped to len) and does not vary; the 'Width' figure is a rolled-vs-unrolled pair where '10in unrolled' is the flat fabric pattern width before rolling (not a usable dimension - would draw a bag longer than the roll itself) and '3.5in rolled' (8.9cm) is the actual packed diameter, used directly for wid/hgt/dia since the cross-section is round. Volume check: a 15.9 x 8.9cm-diameter cylinder is 0.99L, matching the 1L rating almost exactly - strong confirmation this is the right reading.

geometry.notes: Small squat fabric roll, buckled shut lengthwise (not a rolltop with a sealed end - it is a flat tool-roll panel that wraps into a tube). Red-and-white CHROME buckle badge visible on the strap in the on-bike photo. Sits snug against the underside of the saddle and top of the seatpost clamp.

closure.hardware: locking buckle closure that cinches the rolled panel shut; maker copy: 'Locking buckle closure keeps a tight roll under your saddle'

details.fabric: Bluesign approved 1050D nylon with 500D tarp liner - see brand_notes.fabric; the 'tarp liner' is the closest match in this brand's catalogue to brands.json's 'truck-tarp material' claim

mount.notes: Small rigid-feeling roll cinched tight directly under the saddle by a single buckled strap; maker copy says it can also 'stash it in your bag' as an alternative to mounting, but the on-bike photo shows it saddle-mounted.
